domain_setting: A safe, welcoming teaching and research laboratory where learners study living systems, materials, experiments, physical processes, electricity, and magnetism.
global_art_direction: Keep all work grounded in recognizable classroom and laboratory scenes with clear glassware, apparatus, specimens, and safe procedures.
Differentiate neighboring science terms by showing the defining object or physical change, not only a generic scientist or beaker.
Screens, charts, notebook pages, and models may use geometric marks but must contain no letters or numerals.
Show biological and genetic concepts through plants, cells, and transparent models; avoid human subjects or sensational framing.
For material-state verbs, show a visible before/after change in the same vessel or specimen.
Use rounded five-layer SVGs in the Artico palette with clear silhouettes and no text.

entries.biologist: A biologist in a white coat studies a fresh leaf and prepared slide beneath a microscope; frame the work around living organisms.
entries.biology: A living plant, leaf cross-section, and tiny cells under magnification represent the study of life.
entries.chemist: A chemist in safety goggles carefully pipettes liquids into a flask at a clean laboratory bench.
entries.chemistry: A safe color-changing reaction in clear glassware shows substances combining and changing.
entries.physicist: A physicist studies a suspended pendulum beside a magnet and an optical lens, emphasizing measurable physical forces.
entries.physics: A ramp, rolling sphere, light ray, and magnet visualize matter, energy, motion, and forces.
entries.science: A welcoming laboratory combines plant, glassware, microscope, and orbit/force models as ways of studying the natural world.
entries.scientist: Reuse the clear scientist-at-a-laboratory-bench scene from Lesson 34.
entries.battery: A pair of dry-cell batteries powers a simple lamp circuit, making this scientific electrical cell context clear and avoiding a car battery.
entries.beaker: A broad clear laboratory beaker with a pouring lip and measured liquid level on a clean bench.
entries.bunsen burner: A laboratory gas burner with a controlled blue flame beneath a wire gauze and flask.
entries.laboratory / lab: A bright science lab with a long workbench, sink, microscope, glassware, and safety equipment.
entries.microscope: A laboratory microscope with eyepiece, objective lenses, stage, slide, and focus knobs.
entries.mortar: A laboratory porcelain mortar containing ground mineral powder, clearly set among chemistry apparatus.
entries.pestle: A thick laboratory pestle presses dry chemical powder in a porcelain mortar.
entries.safety goggles: Protective wraparound goggles with a clear lens and elastic strap placed beside a lab coat.
entries.test tubes: A rack holds several narrow glass test tubes with different colored solutions and rounded bottoms.
entries.experiment: A controlled plant-growth experiment compares two seedlings receiving different measured conditions.
entries.hypothesis: A researcher forms a tentative cause-and-effect idea before a test, linking a water drop to a possible taller seedling with a dotted prediction path.
entries.observe: A scientist carefully looks through a microscope at a prepared living sample.
entries.record: A researcher records observations as simple sketches, dots, and a blank chart in a lab notebook, with no writing.
entries.result / results: Two finished seedlings and a blank comparison chart show the outcome of an experiment.
entries.test: A gloved hand applies a reagent to a sample strip in a lab test, with a visible color response.
entries.theory: A physical model connects repeated observations into one explanatory system, such as a stable orbit model matching measured paths.
entries.evidence: A labeled-free specimen slide, microscope view, and observation sketch visually support a scientific conclusion.
entries.cell / cells: A plant cell cross-section with membrane, wall, nucleus, and organelles; use the biology sense, not a prison cell.
entries.chemicals: Several clearly distinct reagent bottles with hazard-safe caps and different colored contents on a chemistry bench.
entries.cloning: Two matching plantlets grow from tissue culture in separate sterile jars, showing identical copies in a safe botanical context.
entries.dna: A large colored double helix with paired rungs represents DNA without letters.
entries.genetic engineering: A scientist uses a pipette to insert a highlighted gene segment into a plant cell model, framed as careful agricultural research.
entries.molecule / molecules: A ball-and-stick molecule with bonded colored atoms, clear and number-free.
entries.reaction: Two clear reagents mix and produce visible bubbles and a new color in a flask.
entries.crystals: A cluster of translucent geometric mineral crystals grows from a shallow solution dish.
entries.boil: Water bubbles vigorously in a beaker held above a controlled laboratory burner flame.
entries.burn: A small safe lab sample combusts in a heat-resistant dish with flame, ash, and rising smoke under supervision.
entries.cool: A warm beaker is lowered into an ice bath as its thermometer level falls; no numerals.
entries.dissolve: Solid crystals disappear into stirred water, leaving a clear uniform solution.
entries.evaporate: Water vapor leaves a shallow heated dish and disperses into the air as a liquid-level drop is visible.
entries.float: A cork remains at the surface of water while a denser metal sphere rests below, demonstrating floating.
entries.freeze: A water droplet becomes a faceted ice cube in a cold laboratory dish, with frost forming around it.
entries.gas: Widely spaced particles spread through a transparent chamber, representing a gas state.
entries.heat: A controlled burner warms a flask; heat shimmer and a rising thermometer column show increasing temperature without digits.
entries.liquid: A vivid blue liquid flows to take the shape of a glass vessel while retaining a clear surface level.
entries.melt: An ice cube visibly shrinks into a puddle on a gently warmed dish.
entries.pour: A gloved scientist pours measured blue liquid from a beaker into a receiving flask.
entries.sink (action): A dense metal sphere descends to the bottom of a transparent water vessel, leaving bubbles above.
entries.solid: A solid crystal block keeps a firm fixed shape beside liquid and gas comparison cues.
entries.steam: Visible water vapor curls upward from a hot beaker as droplets condense on a cool glass surface.
entries.attract: Opposite magnet poles draw steel filings and a second magnet toward one another.
entries.electric shock: A small static spark jumps between a protected test probe and a metal terminal in a supervised circuit; no injury.
entries.magnet: A horseshoe magnet lifts several iron paperclips from the bench.
entries.repel: Like poles of two bar magnets push away from one another, shown by their separated ends and outward arrows.
entries.static electricity: A rubbed plastic rod attracts lightweight paper bits and makes a few hairs stand, showing static charge.
